although: Although it was late, the puppy still wanted to play.
I wore my coat, although the sun was shining.
Although I tried hard, the tower of bricks fell down.
experience: Do you have any experience of looking after a pet rabbit?
The new teacher has lots of experience of teaching little children.
Our teacher said we need more experience before we cook alone.
experiment: Let's do an experiment to see if ice melts in the sun.
We mixed paint and water in our science experiment.
The teacher wrote down each result of the experiment.
occasion: We only use the best plates on a special occasion.
Christmas dinner is the one occasion when we all sit together.
On this occasion, we had a picnic indoors because of rain.
opposite: Short means the opposite of tall!
She said yes, but I said the opposite.
The post box is opposite the library.
particular: Only this particular key opens the shed door!
She looked for one particular shell on the beach.
Which particular book do you want from the shelf?
possible: Please tidy your room as soon as possible.
Counting every star in the sky is not possible!
Rain is possible this afternoon, so take a coat.
possession: My bike is my most prized possession.
Her kite is a treasured possession that she keeps in a box.
Every child put one possession in the class box.
accidentally: Oops, I accidentally knocked over the milk!
We accidentally walked past the shop and had to turn back.
Did you accidentally take my coat home?
occasionally: It occasionally snows here, but not every winter.
We eat fish and chips only occasionally, as a treat.
The cat occasionally sits on my lap, but mostly she sleeps.

rejected.s: Why did you wear a hat although it was hot?
rejected.reason: checker: Using although in a question sounds unnatural; 'when' would be the usual word.

rejected.s: Baking bread with Gran was a new experience for me.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: capital word not allowed: Gran

rejected.s: My uncle has years of experience in fixing bikes.
rejected.reason: checker: A man as the one who fixes things is a stereotype we avoid.

rejected.s: Did you enjoy the experience of sleeping in a tent?
rejected.reason: checker: 'The experiment of sleeping in a tent' also makes sense. (also fits: experiment)

rejected.s: She had no experience of snow, so she loved it!
rejected.reason: checker: The 'so' link is weak and hard for a child to follow.

rejected.s: Did the experiment show which paper plane flies furthest?
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: furthest

rejected.s: Mum let me try a baking experiment with no sugar.
rejected.reason: checker: 'No sugar' leans towards diet talk, and Mum in the kitchen is a stereotype.

rejected.s: Your birthday is a happy occasion for the whole family.
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: shares a run of 4 words with the example

rejected.s: Is Eid a happy occasion at your house?
rejected.reason: checker: The question asks the child about religion at home, which we avoid.

rejected.s: Dad made a big cake for the occasion!
rejected.reason: checker: 'Made a big cake for the experiment' also makes sense, and the clue is weak. (also fits: experiment)

rejected.s: What is the opposite of happy?
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: shares a run of 4 words with the example

rejected.s: Please look after each possession when we go swimming.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Each possession' is unnatural; people would say 'your things'.

rejected.s: Is this scarf your possession, or does it belong to me?
rejected.reason: checker: 'Your possession' is awkward; a child would say 'yours'.

rejected.s: She accidentally put salt in the tea instead of sugar.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Occasionally put salt in the tea' also makes sense, so a child cannot tell which word belongs. (also fits: occasionally)

rejected.s: The ball accidentally rolled into next door's garden.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Occasionally rolled' also fits, and a ball cannot act on purpose anyway. (also fits: occasionally)

rejected.s: Mum learned from experience that wellies keep feet dry.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: learned

rejected.s: You learn to ride a bike with practice and experience.
rejected.reason: checker: A child could put 'experiment' after 'practice and', so the gap is not certain. (also fits: experiment)

rejected.s: What a wonderful experience it was to feed the ducks!
rejected.reason: checker: 'What a wonderful occasion' also reads naturally, so the gap is not certain. (also fits: occasion, experiment)

rejected.s: Our street party with flags and cake was quite an occasion!
rejected.reason: checker: 'Quite an experience' also fits naturally, so the gap is not certain. (also fits: experience)
